hook.situation: Your meeting is starting, but your materials are not ready. You need to bring it up, give background, and push the conversation forward without sounding abrupt or defensive.
objectives: Open a sensitive topic with 사실은 and sentence-final -는데요.
Separate new background with -거든요 from shared information with -잖아요.
Use 그런데/근데 to shift or push back while keeping the conversation cooperative.
hook.whyItMatters: A direct translation of 'but' or 'because' often sounds too flat in Korean. These markers show whether the listener already knows the reason, whether you are adding new context, and how much room you are leaving for the other person to respond.

grammarNotes.title: V/A-(으)ㄴ/는데 — background before the main point
grammarNotes.mentalModel: This ending puts a small piece of context on the table before the real point arrives. It is often softer than jumping straight to the request or disagreement.
grammarNotes.formation: Action verbs usually take -는데. Descriptive verbs take -(으)ㄴ데: 가는데, 먹는데, 바쁜데, 좋은데. Past tense uses -았/었는데.

examples.en: The materials are not finished yet, though.
examples.note: Bad news is framed as background, so the listener has space to respond.

examples.ko: 그 의견도 좋은데 시간이 조금 부족해요.
examples.romanization: geu uigyeondo joeunde sigani jogeum bujokaeyo.
examples.en: That opinion is good too, but we are a little short on time.
examples.note: Soft contrast before a practical limit.

examples.ko: 회의는 시작했는데 발표자는 아직 안 왔어요.
examples.romanization: hoeuineun sijakaetneunde balpyojaneun ajik an wasseoyo.
examples.en: The meeting has started, but the presenter has not arrived yet.
examples.note: Connects the situation and the problem.

exceptions: Use -지만 when you want a clearer 'but' contrast.
Use -아/어서 when you are giving a straightforward cause and result.
Do not put action-verb -는데 on adjectives: 바쁜데요, not 바쁘는데요.

grammarNotes.title: V/A-잖아요 — shared information
grammarNotes.mentalModel: 잖아요 says, 'This is already in our shared space.' It reminds the listener rather than teaching them something new.
grammarNotes.formation: Attach -잖아요 to the stem or past form: 바쁘잖아요, 말했잖아요, 주말이잖아요. Casual speech often uses -잖아.

examples.en: The meeting time is short, you know.
examples.note: The short meeting time is treated as shared context.
Can sound pointed if the tone is too strong.

examples.en: The team lead is busy now too, you know.
examples.note: Uses shared information to support a suggestion.

exceptions: Do not use 잖아요 for information the listener could not know. That can sound like you are blaming them for not knowing.

grammarNotes.title: V/A-거든요 — new background or reason
grammarNotes.mentalModel: 거든요 opens a parenthesis for the listener: 'Here is the background you did not have yet.'
grammarNotes.formation: Attach -거든요 to the stem or past form: 늦거든요, 좋거든요, 생겼거든요. Nouns take -이거든요 after a consonant and -거든요 after a vowel in casual flow.

examples.en: Something suddenly came up yesterday, you see.
examples.note: The listener is receiving new context.

examples.ko: 오늘은 먼저 시작해 주세요. 제가 조금 늦거든요.
examples.romanization: oneureun meonjeo sijakae juseyo. jega jogeum neutgeodeunyo.
examples.en: Please start first today. I am running a little late, you see.
examples.note: Explains the request with new information.

examples.ko: 그 카페 자주 가요. 분위기가 좋거든요.
examples.romanization: geu kape jaju gayo. bunwigiga jokeodeunyo.
examples.en: I go to that cafe often. The atmosphere is nice, you see.
examples.note: Gives the reason behind a habit or choice.

exceptions: 거든요 is not a plain substitute for because. It sounds conversational and explanatory.
If the listener already knows the reason, 잖아요 usually fits better.

grammarNotes.title: V/A-는데요 — soft trailing ending
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Sentence-final -는데요 leaves the door open. It can sound like 'here is the situation... what should we do?'
grammarNotes.formation: Action verbs take -는데요. Descriptive verbs take -(으)ㄴ데요: 가는데요, 먹는데요, 바쁜데요, 좋은데요. Past tense uses -았/었는데요.

examples.ko: 사실은 오늘 자료가 아직 다 안 끝났는데요.
examples.romanization: sasireun oneul jaryoga ajik da an kkeunnanneundeyo.
examples.en: Actually, today's materials are not finished yet.
examples.note: A common way to soften bad news before the next step.

examples.en: I am a little busy right now, though.
examples.note: Can be a gentle refusal or hesitation.

examples.en: That method is fine too, but...
examples.note: The listener expects a follow-up contrast or concern.

exceptions: Do not use -는데요 just to make every sentence polite. It should add background, hesitation, surprise, or soft contrast.
A bare -는데요 can feel incomplete without surrounding context.

exampleSentence.ko: 사실은 오늘 자료가 아직 안 끝났는데요.
exampleSentence.en: Actually, today's materials are not finished yet.

exampleSentence.ko: 알겠어요. 그런데 발표 전에 자료는 보내 줄 수 있어요?
exampleSentence.en: I understand. But can you send the materials before the presentation?
exampleSentence.note: Shifts from accepting the situation to asking for the next action.

exampleSentence.en: But that is a little difficult, though.
exampleSentence.note: Casual version of 그런데 for spoken conversation.

exampleSentence.ko: 그러니까 먼저 회의를 시작해도 된다는 말이죠?
exampleSentence.en: So you mean we can start the meeting first, right?
exampleSentence.note: Checks the implied meaning before moving on.

exampleSentence.en: The meeting time is short, you know.
exampleSentence.note: Use when the listener already knows the reason.

exampleSentence.en: Something suddenly came up yesterday, you see.
exampleSentence.note: Use when the listener does not know the background yet.

exampleSentence.en: The materials are not finished yet, though.
exampleSentence.note: Leaves space for the listener to respond.

exampleSentence.en: I will send the materials before the meeting.
exampleSentence.note: The actual file, handout, slide deck, or reference material.

exampleSentence.en: I will explain the background first.
exampleSentence.note: Context that helps the listener understand the situation.

exampleSentence.ko: 상대방이 모르는 내용이면 거든요가 더 자연스러워요.
exampleSentence.en: If the other person does not know it, 거든요 is more natural.
exampleSentence.note: The listener's knowledge decides the marker.

exampleSentence.ko: 그 의견에는 부드럽게 반대하는 게 좋아요.
exampleSentence.en: It is better to disagree with that opinion gently.
exampleSentence.note: Names the tone this chapter is practicing.

exampleSentence.ko: 자료가 늦어진 이야기는 제가 먼저 말을 꺼낼게요.
exampleSentence.en: I will bring up the delayed materials first.
exampleSentence.note: 말 means words or speech here.
A practical verb for giving context.

exampleSentence.en: I agree with that opinion too.
exampleSentence.note: Pairs with 의견 and polite discussion.

exampleSentence.en: I disagree with that opinion a little, though.
exampleSentence.note: Use -는데요 to make disagreement less abrupt.

exampleSentence.en: If you say it like that, the mood becomes a little stiff.
exampleSentence.note: Discourse markers affect the mood of a conversation.

exampleSentence.ko: 상황을 먼저 설명하면 상대방이 이해하기 쉬워요.
exampleSentence.en: If you explain the situation first, it is easier for the other person to understand.
exampleSentence.note: The larger situation tells you which marker fits.

exampleSentence.en: That opinion is good too, but we are short on time.
exampleSentence.note: Natural noun for agreeing, disagreeing, or softening pushback.

extendedDialogue.setting: A team member brings up unfinished materials before a meeting starts.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 사실은 오늘 자료가 아직 다 안 끝났는데요.
lines.romanization: sasireun oneul jaryoga ajik da an kkeunnanneundeyo.
lines.en: Actually, today's materials are not finished yet.
lines.grammarNote: 사실은 plus -는데요 opens bad news without sounding too sudden.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.ko: 그러니까 먼저 회의를 시작해도 된다는 말이죠?
lines.romanization: geureonikka meonjeo hoeuireul sijakaedo doendaneun marijyo?
lines.en: So you mean we can start the meeting first, right?
lines.grammarNote: 그러니까 checks the implied meaning instead of assuming.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.en: Yes. Something suddenly came up yesterday, you see.
lines.grammarNote: -거든요 gives new background the listener did not have.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.ko: 알겠어요. 그런데 발표 전에 자료는 보내 줄 수 있어요?
lines.romanization: algesseoyo. geureonde balpyo jeone jaryoneun bonae jul su isseoyo?
lines.en: I understand. But can you send the materials before the presentation?
lines.grammarNote: 그런데 shifts to the next practical concern.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 네, 그건 가능해요. 회의 시간이 짧잖아요.
lines.romanization: ne, geugeon ganeunghaeyo. hoeui sigani jjaljanhayo.
lines.en: Yes, that is possible. The meeting time is short, you know.
lines.grammarNote: -잖아요 treats the short meeting time as shared information.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: Then I will explain the background first.
lines.grammarNote: 배경 keeps the reason organized instead of sounding like an excuse.

readingText.title: 자료가 아직 안 끝났는데요
readingText.body: 팀 회의에서 자료가 늦어졌다면 바로 '못 했어요'라고만 말하면 조금 딱딱하게 들릴 수 있어요. 먼저 '사실은'으로 말을 꺼내고, '자료가 아직 안 끝났는데요'처럼 상황을 부드럽게 열어 주세요. 상대방이 모르는 이유를 설명할 때는 '어제 갑자기 일이 생겼거든요'가 자연스럽고, 이미 같이 아는 사실을 다시 짚을 때는 '회의 시간이 짧잖아요'가 자연스러워요. 그다음에는 '그런데 발표 전에 자료는 보내 줄 수 있어요?'처럼 다음 행동을 확인하면 대화가 멈추지 않아요.
readingText.bodyTranslation: If the materials are late in a team meeting, simply saying 'I did not do it' can sound stiff. Open the topic with 사실은, soften the situation with -는데요, use -거든요 for new background, and use -잖아요 for shared information. Then move the conversation to the next action.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 자료가 늦어졌을 때 먼저 어떤 표현으로 말을 꺼낼 수 있어요?
상대방이 모르는 이유를 설명할 때 어떤 표현이 자연스러워요?
이미 같이 아는 사실을 다시 짚을 때는 어떤 표현이 자연스러워요?

culturalNote.title: Soft does not mean unclear
culturalNote.body: In Korean, softening a sentence often means preparing the listener for the point, not avoiding the point. A good update still says what happened, why it happened, and what can happen next.
culturalNote.tip: Before choosing 잖아요 or 거든요, ask one question: does the listener already know this reason?

inlineExercises.prompt: The listener does not know why the materials are late. Which ending fits best?
inlineExercises.explanation: Use -거든요 for new background the listener does not know yet.

inlineExercises.prompt: Everyone knows the meeting time is short. Which sentence uses that shared fact naturally?
inlineExercises.explanation: Use -잖아요 when the reason is shared, visible, or already mentioned.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence brings up bad news most softly?
inlineExercises.explanation: 사실은 opens the topic and -는데요 leaves room for the next step.

bullets: 사실은 + -는데요 is useful for opening a sensitive update softly.
-거든요 gives new background; -잖아요 points to shared information.
그런데 and 근데 shift the conversation, but 근데 is more casual.
A soft marker should still lead to a clear next action.
summaryCard.nextChapterTeaser: Chapter 36 moves from softening conversation to reporting what you personally noticed over time.
